newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kazakh net grain harvest at 9 mln T, 75 pct done.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh net grain harvest at 9 mln T, 75 pct done.

text.p: Kazakhstan has harvested a net nine million tonnes of grain so far, with around 75 percent of the Central Asian nation's total grain crop in, a senior Kazakh Agriculture Ministry official said on Wednesday.
"There are already nine million tonnes of threshed (bunkered) wheat in," Abu Baigabulov, head of the ministry's grain department, told Reuters by telephone from the capital Almaty.
Kazakhstan's drought-hit 1995 harvest totalled around 10 million tonnes, and officials had earlier predicted this year's harvest would total 16.5 million tonnes.
Baigabulov said the harvest was mostly of good quality hard wheat.
He said the government planned to buy one million tonnes of Kazakh grain, but gave no details on the price it would pay to farmers.
The Kazakh Research Institute for Grain said rain was hampering the harvest.
But Baigabulov, who said grain yields had averaged around 0.7 tonnes per hectare, played down the difficulties.
"We will finish this," he said, adding, "The rain falls...but the work goes on."

Earlier this month, the official daily Kazakhstanskaya Pravda urged farmers to speed up the harvest to beat forecast rains. Harvesting has already been made difficult by a shortage of combines and other equipment.
